apps.title: Klondike Solitaire
apps.summary: Klondike solitaire: draw one or three, Standard or Vegas scoring.
apps.description: Played by touch or keyboard. Unlimited undo and redo, hints, optional automatic safe moves, a warning when no move is left, numbered deals that are the same on every board and an option for winnable deals proven by a built-in solver. Statistics per variation and the game in progress are kept on the board. No network. Needs a screen of at least 640x480 (portrait 480x640 in PDA mode).

apps.title: Markdown Notes
apps.summary: Notes as plain Markdown files in a folder: write, preview, open by name.
apps.description: Notes are .md files in one folder (~/Notes by default), readable by any Markdown editor and easy to sync with Syncthing, rsync or git (the app does not sync itself). The preview shows headings, lists, code, task boxes you can tick and [[links]] between notes; new notes open in an editor that saves by itself. No network. Best with a Bluetooth or USB keyboard; the on-screen keyboard appears while none is connected.

apps.title: Mesh Hop
apps.summary: MeshCore messenger: chats, contacts and settings of a LoRa companion radio.
apps.description: The deck is the screen and keyboard of a MeshCore companion radio board, over USB, Bluetooth LE or Wi-Fi. Channel and direct chats with search, contacts, nearby nodes, repeater and room login, radio presets and node settings, and the bundled meshcore-cli. Messages are kept per board. Needs a board running MeshCore companion firmware; USB needs the dialout group, Bluetooth needs BlueZ.

apps.title: Mine Field
apps.summary: A mine-clearing puzzle, with fair boards that never need a guess.
apps.description: Dig the safe cells and flag the mines, by touch or keyboard. The board always fits the screen: the three levels are sized from your display. The first dig is always safe, the Fair boards setting lays only boards that logic can finish, and Hint points at a sure cell. Best times, statistics and the game in progress are kept on the board. No network. Needs a screen of at least 640x480 (portrait 480x640 in PDA mode).

apps.title: Net Toolbox
apps.summary: Network tools: diagnosis, ping, traceroute, DNS, speed test, LAN and Wi-Fi.
apps.description: A step-by-step diagnosis of a broken connection in plain words, plus ping, traceroute, DNS lookup, port and HTTP checks, a speed test, public IP, whois, Wake-on-LAN, a Bluetooth radar, a scan of the devices on your network, Wi-Fi networks and channels, a Wi-Fi walk test and the interfaces. No root needed; results can be saved as text. Wi-Fi tools use NetworkManager, the radar needs BlueZ. Works upright in PDA mode.

apps.title: Net Walk
apps.summary: A cable puzzle: turn the tiles until every computer is on the network.
apps.description: Turn the tiles until the server's power reaches every computer. A tap turns a tile clockwise, a long press the other way, a hold locks it. Four sizes: 5x5, 7x7, 9x9 and a 9x9 board whose edges wrap. Best moves and times are kept per size. Touch or keyboard; drawn in a Palm OS colour look that scales crisply to the screen. No network. Needs a screen of at least 480x320 (portrait 480x640 in PDA mode).

apps.title: RSS Reader
apps.summary: A reader for RSS and Atom text feeds, with a catalog of about 260 feeds.
apps.description: Pin feeds from the catalog, by country and topic, or add any site by its address. Read articles full screen with their pictures, in the text size you choose; save articles for offline reading, export or import your favorites as OPML. Only the feeds are fetched, nothing is sent anywhere else. Needs the network to update the feeds; what was fetched stays readable offline. Works upright in PDA mode.

apps.title: Serial Console
apps.summary: A serial console that finds USB-serial adapters and tells what is behind them.
apps.description: Names the adapter or board from its USB ids (FTDI, CP210x, CH340, PL2303, Arduino, ESP32, Pico and more), listens to or, after a confirmation, probes the other end to recognise common firmware and boot loaders, finds the speed and remembers the settings per port. Terminal with a control-key toolbar, logging and reconnect. Needs a USB-serial adapter or board and the user in the dialout group.

apps.title: System Monitor
apps.summary: A live view of CPU, temperature, memory, storage, network and power.
apps.description: Six tiles show the board or PC at a glance, each with a two-minute history; a tap opens a live chart and the details, with the top processes. The Power tile reports under-voltage and throttling on a Raspberry Pi (needs vcgencmd and the video group) and the battery on x86 PCs and tablets. Refreshes every 1, 2 or 5 seconds. Read-only: it changes nothing on the system. No special hardware.

apps.title: viz1090
apps.summary: Live ADS-B aircraft from an RTL-SDR dongle on a world map, full screen.
apps.description: The viz1090 display by Nathan Matsuda with its own readsb decoder. An intro screen checks for the SDR and an optional USB GPS and sets your position. Needs an RTL-SDR dongle with a 1090 MHz antenna. Runs on the deck boards and x86 PCs, upright in PDA mode. Map data: Natural Earth, OurAirports. viz1090: BSD; readsb: GPL-3, source https://github.com/wiedehopf/readsb.
